_authority: How much theory a module carries, and how much must be taught before a trainee is asked anything (L36). The owner, 2026-09-30: 'slide text is too small ... with that low info can [the] topic/ILO be taught?' and 'before [a self-check] there should be enough theory so the trainee can actually do that task and understand it - not 100 words of theory and the task already.' Read by scripts/content_script.py (Stage 3 - every finding is shown on the review page and must be fixed before approval, unless the operator approves despite it, L26) and scripts/make_architecture_page.py (Stage 2 - whether the planned self-checks fit the module's theory time). Change a number here and both follow; nothing else restates them.

slide._why: A slide carries the teaching itself - the facts, numbers, names and reasons the Sub-ILO needs - not a headline for the instructor to fill in. The title counts. Under min_words the slide is too thin to teach from (must fix). Over max_words the room cannot read it from the classroom screen: split it into two slides (a note, not a must - NEW_ENTRANT wants more slides, L28).

notes._why: Owner, 2026-09-30 (2.18.1): the instructor notes are compact - two to four short points, one per line starting '- ' - because they live on the instructor's panel, in the module's own INSTRUCTOR_NOTES.md file, never on a slide. What to ask the room, the one example to give, what to stress. Under min_words there is nothing to go on; over max_words it is a speech, not a prompt - the theory belongs on the slide (both must fix). Before 2.18.1 the floor was 30 words and there was no ceiling.

module._plain_only: Owner, 2026-10-15 (L49, 2.26.0): counted over PLAIN theory only - the slides without "active". A slide where the trainees predict, explain, explore or work an example fills its minutes with what they do, not with words.
module._why: Across a module, the slides' own words plus the instructor notes, divided by the slides' minutes. Under this the module's hours are claimed but not filled: the instructor runs out of material long before the time does (must fix). 25 words a minute, now that the notes are short points and the teaching sits on the slide (2.18.1; it was 40 while the notes were long).

before_self_check._cycles: Owner, 2026-10-15 (L49, 2.26.0): short cycles - about 5 minutes of theory, then the trainees do something. It was 10 minutes and 250 words, which pushed the class toward long plain theory. Active slides count as theory taught here: they teach. That every answer is taught before its question (answers_taught_first) is unchanged.
before_self_check._why: A self-check comes only after a block of new theory: at least this many minutes of slides and this many words (slides + notes) since the module began or since the last task. A module whose theory is shorter than this has no self-check - its module check covers it.

answers_taught_first._why: Every question's correct answer must be found in the slides the trainee has already seen - in their text or the instructor notes - before the task opens. The check compares the correct answer's key words (numbers exactly, words by their first five letters, so Latvian and Russian endings still match) with those slides; under this share of them, the question asks for something not yet taught (must fix). The review page shows, for every question, the slide that teaches its answer.

self_check._why: Enough questions for the trainee's own score to mean something, few enough that the lesson keeps its pace.

module_check._why: Every teaching module ends with one. It covers the whole module, so a short module (under before_self_check.min_minutes of theory) still has one.

split._authority: Owner, 2026-10-15 (L49, 2.26.0): 'now most courses are 80/20 - 80 theory, 20 practical. On paper, in the programmes and IMO model courses it stays as it is. But we want to at least come close to 20/80 - 20 plain raw theory, 80 practical: simulators, active learning theory, self-checks, tablet interactive tasks ... first it needs to be reviewed by the person who uses the plugin.' The programme's hours never change (L1); what changes is how the class spends them. Measured on the Stage 2 page and every Stage 3 review page. A suggestion, not a rule, in 2.26.0.
split._keep_theory: Owner, 2026-10-15: 'still you need enough theory ... that does not mean you don't need raw theory at all, you can still add it, and don't remove existing good theory, because each instructor can skip each slide faster; on paper we have that theory, if someone needs he can read it - but the main teaching activities, how the trainee will gain this knowledge, are in active learning.' So 20/80 is reached with TIME, never by cutting theory: every good theory slide stays (more may be added), its minutes shrink - the instructor moves through it faster and the words stay to be read - and the minutes it frees go to active learning. No suggestion ever says to remove a slide or shorten its text. The slide and density floors still apply.
split._counts: PLAIN = minutes of slides without "active" (the instructor explaining). ACTIVE = slides with "active" (one of the techniques below) + task slides (self-checks, module check, team tasks) + activities (practice, simulator, equipment). Stage 2: plain = the module's theory minutes less its self-checks, module check and the planned theory-as-activity minutes; active = those + the programme's practical minutes.
split._techniques: What makes a SLIDE active - the trainees do something on it, not only listen: explain-then-reveal (they explain first, then the slide shows it), predict-then-reveal (they predict what happens, then see), worked-example (one worked through, then their own attempt), scenario (what would you do), explore (they work the interactive diagram or 3D model themselves - turn it, open it, find the part). The instructor notes say what the trainees do. Marking a slide active that is only shown is not allowed: the operator reads it on the review page.

tablets._law: L35 (owner, 2026-09-30). The course runs on two tablets.
tablets.instructor_tablet: Shows the slides; the instructor terminal mirrors them to the classroom screen through the web view. The instructor notes are on the instructor's panel only. When it is time for a task, the slide on the screen only says that a task starts now and what it is about - the task itself is never on a slide - and the instructor's panel carries one button, OPEN TASK.
tablets.trainee_tablet: Carries only tasks: self-checks, the module check and the final assessment. A task opens on every trainee tablet automatically when the instructor presses OPEN TASK - and only then. The trainee cannot see a list of tasks, cannot browse or open another task, and there is no 'all tasks', 'module tasks' or 'back to tasks' button. One question per screen, Next -> Next; at the end the trainee sees their own score.
tablets.scores: Self-check: the trainee sees their own score, no pass mark. Module check: PASSED or NOT PASSED with the score and the pass mark on the page - for the trainee and the instructor to know whether the module was understood, not an official grade (owner, 2026-10-05, L45). The final assessment is the only official grade.
